A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same induction-head study, with matching authors and three core experiments. The complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-model training experiments using natural, semi-natural, and synthetic data, including induction-head measurements and emergence-point regression.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds larger-model evaluations, alternative behavioral measurements, regression statistics, and cross-validation results.

M1.justification: The emergence predictor changes from T/sqrt(BC) in v1 Appendix D to T/(B^0.37 C^0.62) in v2 Section 5, after testing and dropping a model-size predictor. This refines the existing regression approach; the constrained sampling algorithm and intended matrix-optimization procedure remain intact.

E1.justification: Both versions use English CC100, its bigram-based semi-natural data, and the same nine synthetic Markov configurations. The added measurements evaluate the existing repeated-token copying behavior. Larger sample counts and model configurations change experimental settings rather than dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 5 introduces an explicit comparison between the proposed batch/context regression and a full regression additionally containing model size, evaluated on identical held-out folds. v1 has no corresponding full-versus-reduced comparison. Newly cited methods such as OLMo are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The reported natural-data schedule changes from a 100M-token sample repeated for ten epochs to a 1B-token sample used for one epoch, retaining the 1B-token budget. v2 adds GPT2-125M and GPT2-350M training configurations, logit attribution and associative-recall metrics, and five-fold regression validation using 28 training and seven test models per fold. The schedule revision alone does not establish which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 Section 4 and Appendix J systematically test whether findings from prefix matching persist under logit attribution, recall accuracy, and target-token rank across all three experiments. These analyses reveal metric-dependent exceptions to the dependency finding. The full-versus-reduced regressions also newly test whether model size contributes to emergence prediction.

E5.justification: v1 reports correlation significance and simulated random-attention thresholds but lacks regression-coefficient uncertainty. v2 Tables 3–4 add standard errors, t-tests, p-values, and 95% confidence intervals across four emergence metrics, enabling explicit tests of model-size effects. Neither version reports uncertainty across repeated language-model training seeds.

E6.justification: The expanded PS regression changes batch/context coefficient estimates from -0.51/-0.56 to -0.3689/-0.6155. New Table 5 reports held-out results, including reduced-model PS R-squared values of 0.7653–0.9284. Figures 9–15 add extensive LA/AR results, including strong copying-related outcomes under high-repetition -D conditions despite low PS. The frontier result for Zipf[+D+C] matches v1 Table 1; v2 corrects v1's conflicting prose label.

T1.justification: v2's main emergence equation restores inverse scaling consistent with v1 Appendix D, whereas v1 Equation 1 incorrectly printed multiplication. Appendix H also corrects the duplicated within-category loss to an across-category expression in Equation 21. Most mathematical definitions, the sampling algorithm, and the stationary-distribution entropy derivation are retained; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The three headline contributions remain prediction from batch/context size, a repetition frequency–reliability frontier, and the joint roles of dependency, categories, and marginal distribution. Model-size independence becomes explicit in v2's abstract but was already claimed in v1 Appendix D. The additional validation does not itself redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive discussion of task-dependent emergence, tokenization effects, model-scale limits, and differences between attention, logit contribution, and output accuracy. Crucially, Appendix J.3 acknowledges that constrained sampling violates the intended independence condition and leaves low-PS/high-LA behavior unexplained. These qualifications materially complicate v1's interpretation that local dependency is necessary for induction-head formation.

D1.justification: New Appendix A/Table 2 documents architectural dimensions and training details including learning rate 5e-4, weight decay 0.1, 1% warmup, and cosine scheduling. v2 also specifies Pythia sizes and configurations and supplies a code-access URL absent from v1. These substantially expand reproducibility information beyond the earlier model and checkpoint descriptions.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands research positioning through a dedicated related-work section and new discussion. It distinguishes natural-language pretraining from Zucchet et al.'s sparse-attention task and Park et al.'s Markov-mixture setting, incorporates additional mechanistic and architectural work, and connects the study to broader behavioral and vision phase transitions.

P1.justification: v2 extensively reorganizes the narrative with separate related-work, metric-selection, discussion, and limitations sections. It moves the predictive-law development, category-similarity explanation, and synthetic-distribution summary from appendices into the main text, restructures the appendices, and revises the title and introductory framing.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a two-column main layout, adds metric-development plots and regression tables, and colors the emergence scatterplot by model size. v1's binary Table 1 becomes a graded PS heatmap, while its distribution-statistics Table 3 moves into the main text. The old TWU-normalization Figure 5 is removed, and extensive alternative-metric displays are added.

improvement.justification: v1 relies on PS-centered validation and an in-sample emergence-law fit with limited training documentation. v2 substantially strengthens this foundation through larger-model experiments, held-out regression validation, coefficient uncertainty, and complementary behavioral measurements. Appendix J also exposes an important sampling confound and metric-dependent limitation that v1 overlooks. Remaining inconsistencies, including the normalization constant T and Table 5's R-squared caption, limit precision, but the gains in validation, transparency, and reproducibility constitute a substantial overall improvement.
